$comment: ASK AUTHORITY — which sources Ask may use, and what each of them is entitled to establish.
THIS FILE IS ASK'S, AND ONLY ASK'S. It was split out of registry/sources/current-corpus.json on
2026-08-26 because that file is read by apps/website/src/data/sources.ts to build the /research
page's REPRESENTATIVE list. One file was therefore governing two different questions at once:
what the website shows a reader, and what an agent may assert datumwise's position from. Those
are not the same question and must be allowed to diverge without either one silently moving the
other. /research and /framework are editorial and navigational; this is an authority manifest.
SAME WORDS, DIFFERENT MEMBERSHIP (Huayin, 2026-08-26). A Framework page's Core/Reference lists
mean 'constitutes that framework' / 'useful material around it'. Ask's Core/Reference mean
'entitled to establish the current datumwise position' / 'usable but not independently
constitutive of it'. Heavy overlap is expected. Identity is not, and neither list governs the
other.
THE THREE ENTITLEMENTS:
CORE      — may establish 'datumwise holds ...'.
REFERENCE — may explain, contextualise, develop, compare, or supply implementation detail.
Does NOT independently establish the current datumwise position. This is not a
statement about quality: several reference sources are the HIGHEST authority for
the thing they actually establish. It is a statement about jurisdiction.
EXTERNAL  — not in this file at all, because it is not datumwise material. Describes the
outside world and supports comparison, context and criticism. Never establishes a
datumwise position.
CORE AND REFERENCE ARE GOVERNED SEPARATELY. Each carries its own ruledOn/ruledBy/history, so a
ruling that moves one does not implicitly re-ratify the other.
SEEDED, NOT INVENTED: core[] and reference[] were taken verbatim from current-corpus.json's
`in` and `referenceOnly` as ruled by Huayin on 2026-08-25. This split changes ownership, not
membership. The first divergence between the two files will be a ruling, and it will be
recorded in the history block of whichever set moved.

$comment: What each reference jurisdiction GOVERNS. This is the source-precedence constitution, and it
is deliberately not a linear hierarchy: different sources govern different questions.
Ask enters a reference jurisdiction when the question calls for it, and says which one.
jurisdictions.position: Stances datumwise holds, with their evidence. Explains and applies the research; does not enlarge it.
jurisdictions.normative: The shipped language and system, within their stated jurisdiction. Authoritative for what Columna actually does.
jurisdictions.study: Empirical findings datumwise produced. Governs what the study found, not what the theory holds.
jurisdictions.evidence: What the implementation demonstrably did, generated by running the shipped package.
jurisdictions.defects: Disclosed current defects. Governs what is presently broken or contained.
jurisdictions.teaching: Explains the governing research in plain language. Explains but does not enlarge it.
jurisdictions.prior-research: Earlier or adjacent research, applications and readings. Available when explicitly relevant.
jurisdictions.historical: Preserved prior states. Governs questions explicitly about what was said then.
